quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly. Ease off the throttle and keep going straight. Brake slowly on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the other driver will properly yield to you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Does not mean the driver will properly yield to you.
Means the other driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
Pass on the shoulder instead of the main roadway.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Visibility is more important when riding a motorcycle. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily disappear into another vehicle's blind spot or be missed by drivers.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic around your vehicle.

questions.question: A helmet will not provide the best protection:

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it is free of defects.

questions.explanation: A helmet must meet DOT standards and fit snugly all the way around. It must be free of defects such as cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, you should travel in a:
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles use a staggered formation, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide. A group of three-wheel motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: How can you increase your ability to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride closely to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on and position yourself where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around you so you can avoid hazards. Do not assume eye contact alone will make a driver notice you.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. It is recommended for all riders. Passengers should wear snug clothing so nothing catches on the motorcycle and should lean with the operator when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: Your body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If a person drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks will likely be in their system three hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the hours passed since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. A person who drinks seven drinks in three hours will have about four drinks left in their system three hours later.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a responsible motorcycle rider?

options.text: They can carry out their decisions.

questions.explanation: Responsible riders can ride with awareness, make good decisions, and carry out their decisions. Enjoying riding is not a required characteristic of responsibility.

questions.question: Good motorcycle riders know they are safest when they are:

options.text: On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.explanation: Good riders are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and lane position to stay visible.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Take extra care when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen to riders who have less than six months of experience with their motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding at night, how should your following distance compare to daytime riding?

options.text: Keep a longer distance between you and the vehicle ahead at night.
Keep a shorter distance between you and the vehicle ahead at night.
Always keep the same distance, day or night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance between you and the vehicle ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. Keep a longer following distance when riding at night than during the day.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping a small group of motorcycle riders is:

options.text: A small group is less likely to get separated in traffic.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group is less likely to get separated in traffic.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Compared to large groups, they are easier for other vehicles to pass safely, less likely to be separated by traffic or traffic lights, and create less pressure for slower riders to hurry.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard for other drivers to see at night. A rider should:

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Sound the horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Stay directly in front of other vehicles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes: slowing down, increasing your following distance, using the lights ahead to see farther, using your high beam headlight (unless meeting or following another vehicle), and being flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: Riding alongside another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road surface.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle because it limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: To be effective, an eye or face shield should have all of these qualities, except:
questions.explanation: Effective eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resistant to cracks or breaks, fasten securely, allow clear side vision, and allow air to pass through. They should also fit over eyeglasses if needed. They do NOT need to be airtight.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire will make the steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires immediately.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It works less well than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your face. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
Sit far back on the seat so your arms stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer instead of to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help balance.

questions.question: When riding at night, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid crashes. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road. Use your high beam headlight, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
Your face less well than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes, not your face. A windshield is not an adequate substitute for either.
